name: Cortadrine
manufacturer: Street chemist (Shelf origin, GLMZ South Loop labs)
description: Cortadrine is a rough-synthesized amphetamine-adjacent compound cut with synthetic norepinephrine precursors, produced in Shelf labs as an unlicensed alternative to prescription focus drugs like Clariden. It works — delivering 4-6 hours of driven, aggressive focus — but the synthesis is inconsistent and the side effect profile is severe. It is the focus drug of people who cannot afford the legal alternative and cannot afford not to perform.
side_effects: Cardiovascular strain — elevated heart rate and blood pressure
Severe crash: depression, exhaustion, cognitive fog lasting 8-12 hours
Inconsistent potency batch-to-batch (underdose or overdose risk)
High addiction risk due to crash-driven redosing cycle
Rare: cardiac events in augmented users with chrome cardiovascular components
cultural_context: Cortadrine is the cognitive drug of economic desperation. Tier 1 and 2 workers who need to perform at cognitive levels that their living conditions make impossible reach for it. It's the drug of double-shift workers, Shelf students trying to test their way into Tier 3, and gig laborers paid per task. The crash is brutal and the addiction cycle is well-documented by Shelf harm-reduction orgs that the corponations refuse to fund. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals has lobbied against any legalization pathway that might cut into Clariden's market.
story_hooks: A Shelf community clinic's harm-reduction worker is trying to document Cortadrine cardiac deaths linked to a specific bad batch — and the lab producing it is protected by a gang that doesn't want the heat
A Tier 2 worker has been on Cortadrine for months to keep up with a workload that's designed to require it — and they're starting to suspect this is intentional corporate policy
A character discovers that someone close to them has been quietly using Cortadrine to manage a situation they were too proud to admit was overwhelming them
